status: pre-registered before any design optimisation was run (only the surrogate maps and the fixed references existed)
question: Is there ONE shared V0.5 closure (physical bounds) plus per-pattern actions that the pitcher model can deliver, with which the six patterns still form?

S1.cup: held (default Cup tilt 20 deg, no table)
S1.why: CAD NX as in the pitcher check; the azimuth-resolved outer wall (includes the spout flare) instead of the azimuth mean (the review found the mean optimistic by 4.6-6.7 mm near the spout); the cup held in the hand as in the clips

S2.why: the video gives b = 5 mm (2-8), i.e. the barista's pitcher IS an NX-like short beak (r_tip/R 1.16 vs NX 1.17); S2 with the video's b would duplicate S1, so the task's fallback b = 20 mm (a long pointed latte-art spout, geometry wrapper of the surrogate) is used as the 'what if a pointed spout' hypothesis

S3.cup: held, tilt c(t) from the video per pattern (piecewise linear in clip time, constant outside; layered_heart and push_heart use their own short series), consistent rim (near rim 1 mm above the coffee); maps at 5/10/20/30 deg, linear in c, clamped
S3.why: the surrogate's clearance test takes a static Cup; a time-varying tilt is represented by interpolating maps built at 5/10/20/30 deg. Solver coordinates are NOT stretched (the solver circle = the central 80 mm of the surface, as in S1/S2)
S3.cup_tilt_note: clip time used as V0.5-controls time (both start at the first pour frame / stroke); before the first and after the last measurement the nearest value is held

fixed_closure.why: as FS; no reason to move them (cp physical nominal, beta/nu V0.5's own, not tuned on images)

kappa_r: log, fitted AFTER (B, p) exactly as FS (F-weighted log least squares of kappa_r V_R,w against V0.5's radial target)

pitcher_constant.rule: scanned, NOT fitted per pattern; per spec the alpha with the lowest J_total is reported as the design, the others are reported too

fill_mL.constraint: V(t) = fill - poured volume >= 20 mL (flow maps extended to 20 mL)

z_k.rule: wanted tip height; delivered z(t) = max(z_k, Zreq(t)), Zreq = 0.25 s centred running max of the surrogate z_min(t) at the stream foot, yaw, roll and current fill; z_k solved exactly so that the flow-weighted chi equals the (clipped) target, or the bound if unreachable

s_k.rule: flow scale of the V0.5 controls' F timeline for the stroke (applied to the command BEFORE the 0.08 s spout lag); Q clipped to 1-32 mL/s
s_k.cuts: s = 1 for cut strokes (amended before any optimisation): their chi target (<= 0.03, clipped to 0.02) is reachable by height alone, and their flow sets the cut drag Lambda = kappa_c (1 - chi) S, which the deposit-weighted price (cut deposit ~0.0002) would leave practically free

yaw_k.fixed: atan2(b) of the V0.5 controls' jet b where the direction is not degenerate (|b| >= 0.035 m/s and |b| >= 1.5 x mean hand speed)
yaw_k.free_constraint: reachable from the neighbouring strokes' yaw at <= 300 deg/s (ideal hand) over the gap (bridge duration, or 0.1 s for directly adjacent strokes); the 90 deg/s 'video' hand is checked and reported, not imposed

not_allowed: 5 Hz flow pulsation (pulse = 0 everywhere; a layered_heart variant with the wrist-limited pulsation may be run and is labelled)
changing the V0.5 controls' paths, timings, wiggles

inlet_model.flow: drvf: V0.5-controls F x s_k (taper, 0.1 s ramps, bridges >= 0.3 s) -> first-order spout lag tau = 0.08 s -> Q = clip(F/kappa_Q, 1, 32 mL/s); bridges below 1 mL/s cut
inlet_model.height: --ztr transitions between strokes (<= 0.11 m/s) of the wanted z_k, plus the hand's planned lift L(t) = plan_lift(max(z_min - z_w, 0)) (ideal hand) in the final inlet
inlet_model.U_perp: surrogate: sqrt(v0z^2 + 2 g max(z + dz_origin, 0)), v0z = u0 e_z, u0 = sqrt(2 g max(h_bar, h_k)) from the weir at (Q, V, roll)
inlet_model.u_h: cup frame u = exit (u0 e_h along the spout yaw, roll side component, alpha_lip) + v_hand (= d x_hit / dt as drvf); |u| <= min(0.40 m/s, U_perp) as drvf
inlet_model.footprint: drvf continuity: r = sqrt(Q/(pi U)), aspect hypot(U,|u|)/U, d = 2 sqrt(Q/(|v| pi))

objective.J_total: J_chi + J_s + J_uh + 0.25 J_oth  (pooled over the six patterns; per-pattern and per-stroke contributions reported)
objective.J_chi: sum_k w_k e_k^2 / sum_k w_k, w_k = V0.5 deposit of stroke k (allphys.base_targets 'dep'), e_k = logit(chi_k) - logit(chi_target,k), chi clipped to [0.02, 0.98] (FS's J, unchanged)
objective.J_s: sum_k w_k (0.4 ln s_k / ln 1.25)^2 / sum_k w_k  (a 25 % flow change costs as much as the 0.4 logit 'unreachable' threshold; s is new, it needs a price because it changes the deposit)
objective.J_uh: (1/6) sum_{k in LB} [max(0, ln(kappa_t |u|_k / (0.7 |u|_FS,k)))]^2  -- excess horizontal momentum given to the surface over FS's (FS: kappa_t 0.7, |u| from the stored FS inlet logs), LB = load-bearing strokes of ALLPHYS 6.1
objective.J_oth: sum_{k not in LB} F_k [ln(kappa_t |u|_k / (0.7 |u|_FS,k))]^2 / sum F_k  (two-sided; weight 0.25): keeps kappa_t from absorbing the LB excess by silently removing the cuts' and bases' momentum (FSx showed a larger cut momentum splits the tulip axis; a smaller one is untested)
objective.weights_rationale: logit error 0.4 (the 'unreachable' threshold of allphys) ~ J contribution 0.16 per unit weight share; a 50 % momentum excess on an LB stroke gives ln(1.5)^2/6 = 0.027 per stroke, 0.16 if all six are 50 % over -> both terms of the same order
objective.unreachable: |e_k| > 0.4 at the optimum; reason classified as 'clearance' (z_k pinned at Zreq above the height that would hit the target), 'z bound' (pinned at the class bound), or 'U too low/high'

search.pass1: grid p in {1, 1.5, ..., 8} x 25 log-spaced B_dep in [300, 6000]; kappa_t grid 0..1 step 0.05; inside each: per stroke exact z_k solve (24-point z grid, 16 flow-weighted quantiles of U^2/d per height, linear interpolation in log z) and enumeration of (s, yaw, roll); per pattern enumeration of fill; V(t) depletion with s = 1
search.pass2: fills fixed; V(t) recomputed with the pass-1 s_k; (B, p, kappa_t) re-optimised by coordinate refinement from the pass-1 optimum; combos re-chosen
search.sampling: 10 ms samples of the drvf-style schedule (pulse 0, lag 0.08, ztr) on the stroke's own phase window

screen.patterns: all six per spec + FS at 128^2 as the reference
screen.judge: ana-style structure measures (ref2/structm at h = 1/128) + visual, criteria of ALLPHYS 3.1 (heart: heart + tip; push_heart: arms separate; layered_heart: closed outline, >= 4 bright bands at x = +-0.05 D, curl c95 >= 0.7; tulip: closed, three stacked petals, >= 2 seams at x = +-0.06 D; leaf: >= 5 veins per line, amp >= ~0.15; swan: continuous neck, head, wing texture), judged relative to FS at 128^2
screen.to_256: the spec with the most 'yes' at 128^2; ties -> lower J_total -> S1 before S3 before S2 (S1 is the barista's own pitcher type per the video)

amendments: s fixed at 1 for cuts (before optimisation)

addenda.after: S1 design finished (all alphas), S2/S3 running; nothing of S1 was re-optimised because of this
addenda.sensitivity: S1_V50: S1 with V(t) >= 50 mL instead of 20 mL (the S1 optimum empties the pitcher to 22-43 mL at 78-80 deg; the video's late-pour fill is ~60 mL (20-130) at 72.5-77 deg). Same objective, same grids; reported as a labelled sensitivity, not as a spec; 128^2 screen only if its J or unreachable list differs materially from S1.
addenda.reporting: the video hand (60 deg/s, 2 m/s^2, 90 deg/s yaw) is checked and reported (tilt tracking error, yaw rate), not imposed; the ideal hand (300 deg/s yaw) bounds the free yaws as pre-registered

corrections.after: the first 128^2 screen (v1, kept in design/v1/: S1 6/6 formed, S2/S3 with asymmetric curls in push_heart, layered_heart, tulip)
what: roll: the roll's side exit component u0 sin(roll) sin(alpha_lip) rotated the horizontal jet of FIXED-direction strokes by up to ~24 deg at alpha 20 (S2/S3 chose roll +-20 for J gains < 1e-4) -> this broke the pre-registered rule 'yaw keeps the V0.5 controls' horizontal jet direction where it is load-bearing'. Fixed: roll = 0 for fixed-direction strokes; roll in {-20, 0, 20} only for the free-yaw strokes (whose direction is free anyway). At alpha 0 (S1 v1) the side component is zero, so S1 v1 was not affected by this.

ties: equal-cost yaw / roll candidates were resolved by np.argmin (the first grid value), which put tulip #6 at -165 deg and leaf #4 at -105 deg for no gain (the tulip base white was pushed left). Fixed with a tie-break regulariser 1e-5 x [(angle to the circular mean of the neighbouring fixed strokes' yaw / 90 deg)^2 + (roll / 20 deg)^2] added to the stroke cost (J changes < 1e-4; reported J excludes it).
corrections.unchanged: objective, weights, grids, bounds, fills, alpha scan, closure search, LB set, free-yaw set and windows
